summary: Describes using the Service Location Protocol with TN3270E so that clients can find TN3270E servers and spread sessions across them. TN3270E is how terminal emulators talk to IBM mainframes over TCP. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: If many people want to use the same old-style computer terminals, this helps them find a free one and spreads them out so no single machine gets crowded.

questions: how does slp find tn3270e servers
how does tn3270e session balancing work
subtitle: How a 3270 terminal emulator can find TN3270E servers on its own and pick the least loaded one.

tldr.problem: A TN3270E client normally needs a configured host address and TCP port for the server it connects to, and nothing spreads sessions across several servers.
tldr.mechanism: Servers advertise themselves with the Service Location Protocol (SLP), including a LOAD attribute from 0 to 100 and their LU pools. The client queries SLP, reads the loads and connects to the least loaded server before normal TN3270E negotiation begins.
tldr.outcome: Clients need no fixed server address, and sessions can be spread across servers. How a server computes its load is left to each vendor.

today: RFC 3049 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2001, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The text builds on SLP as specified in RFC 2165, with SLP version 2 (RFC 2608) shown as a forward-looking example.

sections.title: Finding Mainframe Servers with SLP
sections.content:
RFC 3049 describes how to use the Service Location Protocol (SLP) so that a TN3270E emulator can discover TN3270E servers in a network and session balance among them. The RFC defines session balance as the ability of a client to use server load information to connect to the TN3270E server with the least load at that time.

The design follows SLP as defined in RFC 2165, and also gives examples for SLP version 2 (RFC 2608 and RFC 2609) to be forward looking. A client that uses this scheme does not need a configured IP host address or TCP port for its server. It finds the least loaded one with SLP.

The RFC also defines two terms used later. An SNA gateway lets LAN workstations reach SNA hosts and typically includes a TN3270E server. An LU pool is a set of Logical Units that workstations share: the gateway takes an LU from the pool when a session starts and returns it when the session ends.
sections.eli5: Instead of memorising which computer to call, your terminal asks the network who is available and picks the one with the least work to do.

sections.title: SLP Agents in Brief
sections.content:
RFC 2165 gives clients an automatic way to discover services within an administrative domain. Services carry attributes that a client can use to choose among them. SLP has three kinds of agent.

  • User Agents query for services on behalf of an application, based on the service and attributes wanted.
  • Service Agents represent a specific service and advertise it. The service registers its configuration and attribute tag/value pairs with the Service Agent.
  • Directory Agents collect registrations from Service Agents so that User Agents can request them later.

For TN3270E, the service template holds a URL with the server address and port, and the service type, which here is TN3270. The User Agent retrieves service information for the client, looks at the load attribute and can pick the least loaded server. If that server is unavailable by the time the client connects, it can try the next least loaded one on its list.
sections.eli5: There are helpers who know about each server and a notice board that collects their news. Your terminal asks the helpers or the board what is on offer.

sections.title: Server Load and Scope
sections.content:
Servers that provide load information SHOULD include the number of sessions available, meaning not in current use, in the calculation of total load. Other factors may matter too, for example a server that also handles file and print services. The RFC says it is beyond its scope to standardize how load is calculated, because vendors weigh different factors and methods may change over time.

To compensate when servers from different implementations share a network, an administrator can be given a way to adjust the load with an integral number between 0 and 100, 100 being the highest. This acts as an extra factor on the actual load, so the administrator can bias a server up or down in how likely clients are to pick it. A Load attribute MUST be defined for the TN3270E server.

Scope is an SLP parameter used to partition access to servers by clients, which reduces overall traffic as networks grow. Its meaning is set by the administrator, and values often follow departmental, geographical or organizational lines. A server can be assigned one scope or several. A client that is not configured with a scope MUST use the scope default.
sections.eli5: Each server says how busy it is with a number. The shop manager can nudge that number so a big machine gets more visitors than a small one. Scopes are like separate floors of a building, so people only look at the lanes on their own floor.

sections.title: How the Client Picks a Server
sections.content:
The client must allow configuration of an Enable SLP Session Balancing switch, a scope name, a DA discovery time-out and an SA multicast time-out. If balancing is disabled, normal TN3270E telnet negotiation is performed. Both time-outs are in milliseconds. The DA discovery time-out can be zero when the network has no Directory Agents, and the SA multicast time-out applies when requests have to be multicast because no suitable Directory Agent exists.

The sample client flow uses the SLP API calls SLPOpen, SLPFindSrvs, SLPFindAttrs and SLPClose. The client opens a handle, queries for servers, then asks for the LOAD attribute of each server URL such as service:tn3270://9.37.51.254:23. It picks the least loaded server. Discovery happens entirely outside of and before the TN3270E telnet negotiation.

The SLPv1 query string has the form TN3270/<scope name>/LUPOOL/ == <pool name><TAB><device type>. The pool name is 1 to 8 upper case characters, and the same pool name must be configured on the different servers. In SLPv2 the scope and service type become separate fields (service:TN3270), and a scope is always required, with DEFAULT used if none is known.
sections.eli5: Your terminal asks, "Who has a free seat of the kind I need?", checks how busy each one is, and goes to the quietest. Only then does the normal hello between terminal and server start.

sections.title: Device Types and Pool Queries
sections.content:
The device type in a query narrows the search to pools that offer the kind of 3270 terminal the client wants. The RFC maps these codes to TN3270E device types.

An example given is a client searching the ENGINEERING scope for a model 2 screen and pool POOL2, which produces the request TN3270/ENGINEERING/LUPOOL/ == POOL2<TAB>3270002.

The client can also compare loads directly. If an attribute request for LOAD returns values such as 35, 88 and 78, the client can then issue a service request for servers with LOAD<40. Even if loads change in between, the client still gets the best the network has to offer.
sections.eli5: You can say what kind of screen you need, and you can even say "only show me servers that are less than 40 percent busy".

sections.title: Client Recommendations and Failover
sections.content:
The client SHOULD display the IP hostname and TCP port in use, so the user knows which server the session is on. It SHOULD also display the resource name returned by the server after negotiation, which tells the user which LU in the pool is in use.

If the connection to the chosen server fails, the connection should be closed and the client should try other servers in its list of least loaded servers. A server may reject a connection, for example when the pool is full or when the device type does not match what the pool holds. In that case an attempt to other least loaded servers SHOULD be made.

The RFC includes an informational trace: an SLP request for pool POOL2, two service replies, a connection to the first address on port 23, and then the normal TN3270E exchange with DO TN3270E, WILL TN3270E and a DEVICE_TYPE REQUEST.
sections.eli5: If the quietest lane turns out to be closed, you just walk to the next quietest one.

sections.title: Service Templates and Registrations
sections.content:
Service templates formally define the attributes of a service, using the grammar of RFC 2609. RFC 3049 defines two. The service:tn3270 template (type tn3270e, version 1.0) carries attributes including:

  • load, an integer from 0 (lowest possible load) to 100 (highest)
  • LUPool, pool names with the device types each supports
  • keywords BIND, DATA, RESPONSES, SCS and SYSREQ for supported TN3270E functions, plus RFC1576, RFC1646 and RFC2355
  • security (values NONE and SSLV3) and Ciphersuites
  • platform, protocol, server name and release

The second, service:commserver, describes the generic attributes of the server: platform, protocol, server name and release. It is registered whenever the communications software is loaded on the server. The RFC also gives sample registration messages for both.
sections.eli5: A template is a form every server fills in about itself: its name, how busy it is, what kinds of terminals it offers and how secure it is.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
SLP can help clients discover the security services a TN3270E server supports. If security is important or required, the RFC recommends SLP authentication and, in SLP version 1, protected scopes.

Templates tell clients how to interpret service information. If templates are modified or false ones distributed, services may fail to register correctly or clients may be unable to interpret what they receive. Service URLs could also be distributed to point at a service other than the one normally wanted. SLP offers an authentication mechanism that lets the URLs of registered services be signed and the signatures verified by clients.
sections.eli5: If someone puts up a fake sign pointing to the wrong lane, you could end up in the wrong place. SLP lets signs be signed, so you can check they are real.
